lines.trans: Close your mouth, Samsonov, you'll catch a draft!
Did you count to ten?
Yes, I counted all of it.
Nothing terrible, that is logical.
This is the first stage: denial.
What? What denial?
Don't worry about it.
When you are leaving home...
Don't forget to kiss the children.
Say: I am always your dad.
Got it, I will kiss them and say it.
And where do I go afterwards?
To my hotel, Samsonov!
There we will continue the operation.

examples.text: Ладно, поезжай в гостиницу, ты устала.

Disbelief. Core Russian part meaning 'yes' in everyday speech.
followed by the genitive plural: 'десять минут'

examples.text: Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: All right, stay there. I'll be there in ten minutes.

examples.trans: There's a new building on Simashko Street.

examples.text: Квартира будет отличная. На Симашко есть новый дом.
examples.trans: It'll be an excellent flat. There's a new building on Simashko Street.

досчитать.gloss: to count up to, finish counting

meanings.en: to count up to a number
meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'считать'). Used as an verbal verb meaning 'to count up to, finish counting'.

examples.trans: Yes, I counted all of it.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'быть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forget', paired with 'забывать'.

examples.trans: Don't forget to wash the toilet.

examples.text: Сейчас будешь чинить трубу. И унитаз не забудь помыть.
examples.trans: Now you're going to fix the pipe. And don't forget to wash the toilet.

meanings.note: A door, a shop, or a legal case. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'крыть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to close, to shut', paired with 'закрывать'.

examples.text: А потом, Аркадий Борисович, мы закроем ваше дело.
examples.trans: And then, Arkady Borisovich, we will close your case.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: In one direction, now. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (on foot)', paired with 'пойти'.
To run for a second term. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (on foot)', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: + dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'to, towards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: In questions. Core Russian det meaning 'what; what a' in everyday speech.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Question word and conjunction. Core Russian adv meaning 'when' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: When I grow up, I'll be the mayor.

meanings.note: For movement; где is for location. Core Russian adv meaning 'where (to)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Wait, where are you two going?

meanings.note: Short form: логично. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('logical').
нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'всегда').

examples.trans: Say that you are leaving for good.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.

examples.trans: Just look at these Moscow types, Lieutenant. And they're the ones who mess up operations.

meanings.note: Первая стадия — отрицание. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'рицание'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'denial, negation' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is the first stage: denial.

meanings.note: С первого раза = the first time. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('first').

examples.text: Ты не понимаешь с первого раза?
examples.trans: You don't understand the first time?

examples.text: Ты что, с первого раза не понимаешь?
examples.trans: What, you don't understand the first time?

meanings.note: Понял? = got it?; понял = got it. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to understand', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'then, later, afterwards' in everyday speech.

A business, conversation, or work. Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'должить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to continue, to carry on', paired with 'продолжать'.

examples.text: Галя, если бы ты моё дело продолжила!
examples.trans: Galya, if only you had continued my business!

examples.text: Он хотел, чтобы она его дело продолжила.
examples.trans: He wanted her to continue his business.

продуть.gloss: to blow through; catch a chill/draft

meanings.note: impersonal: продует = you'll catch a draft

Game or match. Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'дуть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to blow through; catch a chill/draft'.

examples.trans: Close the window, you'll catch a draft.
Close your mouth, Samsonov, you'll catch a draft!

meanings.note: Plural: дети. Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'child' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Самсонов, рот закрой! Зачем ты его обижаешь?
examples.trans: Samsonov, shut your mouth! Why are you insulting him?

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

Polite request. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

meanings.note: Стадия отрицания = stage of denial. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тадия'). Common feminine noun meaning 'stage, phase' in everyday Russian.
